comparison: Both strongly support the primary null findings regarding aperiodic EEG differences between chronic pain and healthy groups (C5, C39-C41) and lack of correlation with pain intensity (C6, C42-C44). OpenEval emphasizes Bayesian statistics and multiverse analysis robustness; peer reviewers describe findings as 'compelling' and 'convincing' with no methodological concerns raised.

Both support the correlation analysis null findings (C6, C42-C44). OpenEval provides detailed statistical justification (BF10=0.103, specification curve analysis); peer reviewers confirmed 'no correlation between the aperiodic component and pain intensity' without raising concerns.

Both support CBP subgroup findings (C7, C49-C50). OpenEval notes 46/48 specifications showed null evidence and matched control design strengthens comparison; peer reviewers confirmed results were 'consistent across various chronic pain subtypes' without specific concerns about CBP analysis.

Both acknowledge uncertainty in CWP findings (C7, C51-C52). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to small sample (N=33) and heterogeneous multiverse results; peer reviewers accepted subgroup consistency but did not specifically address CWP limitations, focusing instead on overall subgroup robustness.

Both support whole-brain analysis findings (C8, C53-C54). OpenEval emphasizes FDR correction and consistent null results across 100 regions; peer reviewers confirmed findings were 'corroborated by whole-brain analyses' without methodological concerns.

Both strongly support the main conclusion (C9-C10, C78). OpenEval emphasizes convergent evidence from multiple analysis types; peer reviewers described results as 'clear and conclusive' and 'compelling evidence,' explicitly accepting the negative finding as scientifically valid and important.

Both support exploratory aperiodic offset findings (C45-C46). OpenEval notes moderate Bayesian evidence for null but acknowledges less rigorous methodology than preregistered analyses; peer reviewers did not specifically discuss these findings but raised no concerns, implicitly accepting them.

Both strongly support methodological rigor (C4, C34-C37, C80-C110 vs C9, C34-C37, C40-C41, C43-C44). OpenEval comprehensively evaluates all methodological aspects including preprocessing; peer reviewers explicitly praised preregistration, multiverse analysis, blinding, and open science practices, describing the study as 'well-designed and rigorously conducted.'

Divergent evaluations of data pooling and sample characteristics (C80-C97). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, noting appropriate sample sizes and transparent reporting; peer reviewer initially rated UNCERTAIN, identifying pooling across protocols as a weakness that 'increases sample variability,' though concerns were later addressed in revisions.

Divergent evaluations of preprocessing and source localization (C98-C108). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED with 'well-documented' quality control; peer reviewer rated UNCERTAIN, noting source estimation 'may yield imprecise results' with default models, though concerns were addressed in revisions and the inherent limitation acknowledged.

Divergent evaluations of aperiodic exponent as E/I proxy (C3, C21-C30). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, noting claims are 'well-supported by citations to foundational work'; peer reviewer rated UNCERTAIN, questioning whether 'this measure may not be the most accurate or optimal for quantifying E/I balance,' though authors addressed this limitation appropriately.

OpenEval evaluated the scientific rationale and literature review (C1-C2, C11-C20) as SUPPORTED with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers did not specifically comment on the introduction or literature review quality.

OpenEval evaluated the mPFC-focused hypothesis (C31-C33) as SUPPORTED with appropriate justification from animal studies. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers did not specifically comment on hypothesis formulation.

OpenEval evaluated the discussion of alternative explanations (C55-C69) as SUPPORTED, noting balanced consideration of methodological limitations and clinical heterogeneity. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers did not specifically comment on the discussion section quality.
